newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 20.

text.p: The government and ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) plan to set up an independent watchdog for financial institutions that is separate from the Ministry of Finance (MOF). The government and LDP may adopt the idea of setting up a bureau attached to the prime minister's office and headed by a cabinet minister.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) wants an organisation for inspecting financial institutions to be similar in status to the national tax agency or under the MOF's control.

The MOF will revise standards for calculating the capital-risk ratios of securities companies, in line with the plans for a "Big Bang" to liberalise Japan's financial markets unveiled by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
A top bureaucrat at the Health and Welfare Ministry resigned on Tuesday amid reports that he took cash and other gifts from a business executive.
